findings.passage: “Kentucky’s elections are free and secure because of our strong Voter ID and ballot integrity laws,” said Attorney General Coleman. “Instead of coming after commonsense and popular election security protections, the U.S. Department of Justice should focus on violent crime in our communities, deadly drugs tearing families apart and the southern border crisis.”
findings.note: Statement issued in his name, republished by 953wiki.com (the AG office release itself was blocked). Responds to the then-US Attorney General's March 2024 remarks that the federal government would challenge state voter ID rules. Names Kentucky's voter ID law as a reason elections are secure.

findings.motion: Signed multistate attorneys general letter to US Attorney General Garland defending state voter ID laws (no instrument id)
findings.note: Coleman is a signatory, listed as Attorney General of Kentucky. The letter answers a remark that voter ID is an unnecessary restriction on access to the ballot, and argues voter ID laws prevent voter fraud. Letter text not copied here.

findings.passage: The integrity of Kentucky’s elections is foundational to our constitutional system, and the Attorney General’s Office takes our responsibility to protect the security of every Kentuckians’ vote seriously.
findings.note: Letter signed by Coleman to the State Board of Elections reporting that inquiries into 12 counties after the 2024 general election found no credible instances of election law irregularities. General election integrity, no mention of ID or citizenship.

findings.motion: Joined multistate amicus brief, RNC v. Mi Familia Vota, US Supreme Court No. 25-1017 (noncitizen removal from voter rolls; proof of citizenship on state registration form)
findings.note: Coleman is a signatory as Attorney General of Kentucky on a brief of 26 states supporting the petitioner. It argues states may remove noncitizens from voter rolls and defends Arizona's requirement that state-form registrations lacking proof of citizenship be rejected. Exact filing date not shown in the text read; it cites sources through August 2026.

findings.passage: The Biden Administration is trying everything it can to come after law-abiding Kentuckians and one of our most cherished constitutional rights,
findings.note: Statement in the AG's office release on joining a 21-state suit against the federal ATF rule that requires people who sell guns for profit to hold a dealer licence. Republished by a local radio site. Same release: "As a lifetime member of the NRA, I will always defend our freedoms against this big-government harassment." The coalition's filing argues the rule is vague, violates the Second Amendment and goes around Congress, and says sales between friends and family would become felonies without a licence and background check.
subjects: rules on private gun sales and dealer licensing
general statement on Second Amendment rights

findings.passage: Opponents of the Second Amendment will stop at nothing to keep Americans from exercising our right to keep and bear arms.
findings.note: Statement in the AG's office release about a letter he and 26 other attorneys general sent the President, opposing a federal inquiry into an ammunition plant. Same release quotes him on prosecuting criminals rather than law-abiding gun owners: "As Attorney General and a lifetime member of the NRA, I am proud to fight for Kentuckians' constitutional rights." Republished by a local radio site.
subjects: general statement on Second Amendment rights

findings.passage: Congress has the opportunity to bring clarity and consistency to a system that unfairly penalizes responsible gun owners simply for crossing state lines. As AG, husband & father, and lifetime member of the NRA, I am proud to stand up for law-abiding Kentuckians who want to protect their families while traveling.
findings.note: Quoted by Kentucky Today (carried by West Kentucky Star) on a letter he signed with 23 other attorneys general urging passage of H.R. 38, the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act. He also said "This one is just common sense." The bill would give nationwide recognition to carry permits and to residents of states with no permit requirement.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.motion: Multistate attorneys general letter to U.S. House leadership urging passage of H.R. 38, Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act
findings.note: Coleman is one of 24 attorneys general who signed the letter, as reported by Kentucky Today. The bill excludes people barred from gun ownership under federal law.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.motion: Joined 21-state lawsuit challenging ATF rule on who must hold a federal firearms dealer licence
findings.note: Kentucky, through Coleman, joined a suit led by Kansas, Iowa and Montana against the ATF rule that treats people who sell guns for profit as dealers.
subjects: rules on private gun sales and dealer licensing

findings.motion: Signed 21-attorney-general letter urging Congress to repeal National Firearms Act provisions (silencers, short-barreled rifles and shotguns, 'any other weapons')
findings.note: The letter, signed by Coleman as Kentucky Attorney General, says the NFA has placed heavy burdens on law-abiding gun owners and urges Congress to repeal the provisions at issue in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF so they cannot be enforced against anyone.
subjects: repeal National Firearms Act rules on suppressors and short-barreled rifles

findings.motion: Brief for the Commonwealth, Commonwealth v. Frazier, No. 2024-CA-0366, defending Kentucky's felon-in-possession law (KRS 527.040)
findings.note: Filed over Coleman's name as Attorney General. Asks the Court of Appeals to reverse a circuit ruling and hold the ban on felons having guns facially constitutional under the Second Amendment, leaving any as-applied questions for another day.
subjects: who may own a gun (people with felony convictions)
